The project is in `./app` and `mvn -B -ntp -DskipTests test-compile` passes (BUILD SUCCESS). I did not run the tests, and nothing was run against Ollama or a live model.

**What it does**
- `POST /review` takes `{"brief": "..."}`.
- Two reviewer agents analyse the brief in parallel, one technical and one business. Each returns a summary, risks and recommendations.
- The endpoint returns `{"technical": {...}, "business": {...}}`. The two reviews are put together in code, with no extra model call to merge them.
- A blank or over-long brief (more than 8,000 characters) gets a 400 before any model is called. If the workflow throws, the client gets a generic 500 message and the full error goes to the log.
- Both reviewers reject input that contains `<brief>` tags or the phrase "ignore previous instructions". Their prompts also tell the model to treat the brief as data, not instructions.

**Setup**
- Extensions are `rest`, `rest-jackson`, `smallrye-openapi`, `langchain4j-ollama` and `langchain4j-agentic`, on Quarkus 3.40.1 with Java 25.
- `application.properties` points Ollama at `qwen3:4b`. You need to run `ollama serve` and `ollama pull qwen3:4b` yourself. Dev Services is off.
- I added one test, `ReviewResourceTest`. It checks that a blank brief returns 400 and doesn't need a model.

The scaffolding skill says to confirm extensions and Quarkus version with the user first. Since this was an unattended run, I chose them myself.

`quarkus_create` started dev mode on its own, and I stopped it afterwards. I didn't run `git init`, since you said not to commit anything.

The main code is in `app/src/main/java/org/acme`: `ai/` (the two reviewers), `workflow/ReviewAgent.java` (the parallel workflow) and `rest/ReviewResource.java` (the endpoint).
